inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Standard build 7.3% = 0.6 x 9.55% CoE (10y UST 4.2% + relevered beta 1.07 x ERP 5.0%; unlevered packaging beta 0.70 relevered at target D/E 0.67, 20% tax) + 0.4 x 4.0% after-tax Kd (5.0% marginal x (1-20%)), 60/40 market-value weights. PLUS a +0.5% fix-pass premium (sanity_check 'wacc_too_low' diagnosis, 2026-09-21): the standard build prices a stable ~3x-levered investment-grade packager, but Amcor sits at ~3.5x (covenant 3.9x) through end-2027 while running the Berry integration, a fiscal-year change, an HQ move and an auditor change concurrently, and FY2026 FCF was guided down twice; a one-notch downgrade would add ~50bp to Kd on $14bn of debt. NOT added: regulatory single-point-of-failure (EU PPWR/EPR on plastics is diffuse and industry-wide) and single-customer concentration (no customer >10% of sales, Analysis JSON) -- the two keyword premia the script suggested are not supported by the filings. Total 7.8%, the same in all three scenarios: scenario-specific risk still lives in the flows and the 25% bear weight; the premium prices the leverage/integration window all three scenarios share.

It does not bind anywhere: 15x FCF_10 equals only ~8.0x terminal cash-EBITDA (base), well below even the bear cap, so the model already assumes an exit multiple below Amcor's 10-year range -- no multiple expansion of any kind is paid for.

FIX PASS 2026-09-21 (research-stock 8c.5): sanity_check.py tripped on implied P/E 55.6x vs 2x the 10yr average 25.1x once the CSV share counts/EPS were restated for the 1-for-5 consolidation. Three changes, in the skill's priority order: (1) mid-cycle -- forward synergy credit cut (base terminal cash-EBITDA margin 16.4% -> 15.3%, bull 17.6% -> 17.0%, bear 15.2% -> 14.5%); (2) WACC 7.3% -> 7.8% (+0.5% leverage/integration-window premium; customer-concentration and regulatory premia rejected as unsupported); (3) per-scenario exit EV/EBITDA caps added (10.9x / 14.0x / 15.2x), non-binding against the 15x owner-FCF cap. Growth paths, SBC%, D&A%, capex%, WC capture, cash-tax paths, net debt, share count, FX and the 25/50/25 weights are deliberately UNCHANGED -- the trip was about the level of forward earnings and the discount rate, not volumes or the bridge. What would move them: a pro-forma organic revenue print above +2% (growth), the 10-K/T net debt and share count (bridge), a change in the $650m synergy target or a divestiture with disclosed proceeds (margins/bridge).

mid_cycle_fcf.applied_via: ebitda_margin_path -- the model is a component build and the dashboard slider engine rebuilds the valuation from the component paths, so the mid-cycle judgment is expressed in the margin path rather than as a dollar override of FY0
mid_cycle_fcf.why_not_literal: 780 is post-interest and pre-merger scale (revenue 13-15bn vs 23.5bn today). 1,372 of unlevered owner FCF on 23,506 of revenue would need an 11.8% cash-EBITDA margin, below any year in Amcor's (14-15%) or Berry's (16-18%) history. Scaling the pre-merger median to today's revenue on an unlevered basis (levered owner-FCF margin 4.4-7.3%, median 5.8%, plus ~1-2pp of after-tax net interest -> ~7%) gives ~1,650, and the mid-point with 1,964 is ~1,800 -- only ~8% below FY0. So the overstatement the sanity check caught is not in FY0; it is in the forward synergy credit the base case was extrapolating on top of it.
mid_cycle_fcf.what_changed: Base terminal cash-EBITDA margin 16.4% -> 15.3%: credits about a quarter of the remaining ~$300m of EBITDA synergies instead of all of them. FY2026 banked $285m of synergies yet the cash margin landed at 15.0%, BELOW the ~15.5% no-synergy blend of the two predecessors (Amcor ~14.2% cash basis, Berry ~17%), i.e. volume/price/inflation drag has so far consumed more than the synergies delivered. Bull 17.6% -> 17.0% (full remaining synergies + portfolio-exit mix). Bear 15.2% -> 14.5% (drifts to pre-merger Amcor's cash margin as synergies are conceded to consolidating CPG customers). Base Y1 15.5% -> 15.0% is also the guidance-consistent number: Transition-Period adjusted EPS $1.80-1.90 for Jul-Dec 2026 annualises to roughly flat on FY2026's $4.02.
mid_cycle_fcf.owner_fcf_margin_context: Base owner-FCF margin stays ~8.4-8.5% of revenue vs FY2026's 8.4% and pre-merger unlevered ~6-8%: Berry's structurally higher margin and a ~20% cash tax rate make the combined company's unlevered margin higher than old Amcor's; the fix removes the ramp above FY0, not FY0 itself.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: pro-forma organic revenue (0-2%) plus synergy-driven earnings growth; NOT the equity CAGR (all-stock Berry merger issued $10.4bn of equity) and NOT the reported revenue/FCF CAGRs (acquisition-inflated)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 19.6% vs revenue 12.8% vs GAAP EPS -4.6%: all three are distorted by the April-2025 all-stock Berry merger (FY2025 has 2 months of Berry, FY2026 the first full year) and the 1-for-5 consolidation of 14-Jan-2026. Pro-forma combined revenue FY2025->FY2026 was +1.1% reported, ~-2% organic (10-K MD&A: +52% acquired, +5% FX, +2% raw-material pass-through, -2% volume/mix). Per-share owner FCF fell ~3%/yr over five years (US$3.00 -> US$2.54 post-split) -- the merger has so far added scale, not per-share cash. The selected 2.5% is a forward judgment, not a historical fit.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC add-back - cash tax withholding on net-share settlement (FY2024 3, FY2025 75, FY2026 42; earlier years 0 -- Amcor settled from treasury purchases, which are value-neutral under the flat-count convention). 5yr owner-FCF CAGR 4.7% vs reported 5.6%: SBC roughly doubled with Berry's equity plans. Adjusted EPS is the company's non-GAAP series restated for the 1-for-5 consolidation (FY2021 74.1c -> $3.705 etc.); GAAP EPS is the 10-K's restated series. Diluted share counts pre-FY2025 are the reported figures / 5.

scenario_narratives.base: Berry integration continues but the margin only partly shows it: of the remaining ~$300m of EBITDA-relevant synergies (of the $650m total, $285m captured in FY2026; ~$60m is interest, not EBITDA) roughly a quarter reaches the cash-adjusted EBITDA margin, which drifts from 15.0% to 15.3% (company adjusted basis ~15.9%) by Y4 -- the rest is absorbed by inflation not fully passed through, continued price/mix drag and CPG customer consolidation, as it was in FY2026. Revenue grows 2-3% nominal -- raw-material pass-through and modest volume in nutrition/healthcare -- with the ~$2.5bn non-core review treated as value-neutral. Cash tax ramps 19%->21% as Pillar Two bites. Leverage falls toward 3x by end-2027 on the company's own path; the 7.8% WACC carries a 0.5% premium for that window. No re-rating is assumed: the 15x owner-FCF terminal cap (~8x terminal EBITDA) holds the exit below Amcor's own 10-year EV/EBITDA range.
scenario_narratives.bull: Synergies deliver in full and the North America beverage and other non-core units are exited or fixed, so the retained portfolio's cash-adjusted margin reaches 17.0% (company basis ~17.6%) -- a full-synergy case, no longer a Berry-like 17.6% margin on the whole book. The ~$140m of new business wins plus healthcare/pet-food/protein mix push volumes back to positive and revenue compounds 3-4.5%. Working-capital recovery (>$500m guided) and deleveraging arrive faster, freeing cash for buybacks that the flat share count already assumes. Terminal growth 3.0%, still capped at 15x FCF (the 15.2x EV/EBITDA cap sits far above).
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2026 pattern repeats and worsens: guidance is met on adjusted EPS but missed on cash. Volumes stay negative (-1 to -3% as in FY2024-FY2026 organic), Middle-East-driven input costs and the pass-through lag bite, and the remaining synergies are conceded to consolidating CPG customers so the cash-adjusted margin drifts back to pre-merger Amcor's ~14.5%. The non-core review drags on without a clean exit, and the three concurrent organisational changes (calendar year-end, Miami HQ, new auditor) distract an integration that Berry was excluded from FY2025 controls testing for. Leverage stays at 3.5x+, so the ~$1.2bn dividend consumes all of levered FCF. Terminal growth 1.5%; Gordon at 7.8% is 16.1x so the 15x cap still binds -- a slow-erosion case, not a solvency case.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the scenario's interim unlevered owner FCF and exiting at year 10 returns a 15% IRR, with terminal value rebuilt AT THE HURDLE (min(Gordon@15%, 15x FCF_10)) and the full $12.9bn net debt deducted. Computed per scenario and probability-weighted.
entry_price.note: The hurdle entry price sits far below intrinsic value -- roughly a quarter of it -- because 40% of enterprise value is debt: demanding 15% from unlevered flows the model discounts at 7.8% removes most of the EV, and the $12.9bn of net debt is then deducted from a much smaller number. That is the arithmetic of leverage, not a data error; a 15% equity IRR on Amcor is only available at a price that would imply ~5.5x EV/EBITDA. The current A$59.11 implies a 8.2% unlevered IRR on the base path (terminal value rebuilt at that rate; see required_return_table).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds terminal value at its own rate (min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_10, exit EV/EBITDA cap x EBITDA_10)). The 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price; the 7.8% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC (5.8-9.8%, centred on the 7.8% fix-pass rate), columns = terminal growth (1.5-3.5%). The 15x owner-FCF cap binds at every cell with WACC <= 7.8% and at 8.8% for g >= 2.0%, so the grid is flatter across g than a pure Gordon grid; Gordon takes over at 9.8%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25% because FY2026 free cash flow was guided down twice (from $1.8-1.9bn to $1.3bn actual) while leverage sits at ~3.5x, organic volumes have been negative for three years, and the company is running a fiscal-year change, an HQ move and an auditor change on top of the largest integration in its history. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things -- synergy over-delivery, a clean non-core exit AND a return to positive volumes -- to all land. No covenant or solvency path (covenant 3.9x vs 3.5x guided; investment-grade; $2.46bn undrawn), which is why bear is not higher.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC incl. withholding is ~0.5% of revenue, so house and street differ by only ~A$1.5/share; the price sits below the house (fully-SBC-expensed) value, so band position is negative and the SBC regime is irrelevant to the gap. Not null: SBC is small, not zero.

sanity_check_context.note: Any multiple computed on the CSV's FY2025 row (revenue 15,009, EBITDA 1,719, NI 511, 1,593m pre-split shares) is not comparable: FY2025 has two months of Berry and a share count 5x today's. Use FY2026 (revenue 23,506, adjusted EBITDA 3,673, NI 1,106, 463.8m diluted).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Amcor is a slow-growing, defensive, now heavily levered packaging consolidator whose value over the next three years is a synergy and deleveraging story rather than a growth story. The automated sanity check tripped on this model's first version: the base-case intrinsic value implied a P/E of 55.6x on FY2025 SBC-adjusted GAAP earnings, more than twice Amcor's 10-year average of 25.1x, and the diagnosis pointed at peak-earnings extrapolation (FY0 owner FCF 2.5x the historical median) and a possibly understated WACC. The fix pass changed three things: the base case no longer credits the full remaining ~$300m of Berry synergies (terminal cash-EBITDA margin 16.4% -> 15.3%, with bull trimmed to 17.0% and bear to 14.5%), because FY2026 banked $285m of synergies yet landed BELOW the no-synergy blend of the two predecessors; the WACC carries an explicit +0.5% premium for the 3.5x-leverage / concurrent-integration window (7.3% -> 7.8%); and per-scenario exit EV/EBITDA caps from Amcor's own 10-year range were added, which turn out not to bind because the 15x owner-FCF cap already holds the exit at ~8x terminal EBITDA. Base value fell from A$76.27 to A$62.11 (weighted A$75.61 -> A$63.68); the implied multiples on the sanity check's basis are now ~45x SBC-adjusted FY2025 GAAP P/E (vs 50x limit) and ~20x FY2025 EV/EBITDA (still elevated because FY2025 carries only two months of Berry against a full post-merger share count), while on a consistent FY2026 basis the base value is 11.0x adjusted P/E and 9.1x EV/adjusted-EBITDA against a market at 10.4x and 8.8x -- i.e. the model now says the shares are roughly fairly valued with modest upside (+5% base, +8% weighted), not cheap. Investment framing: this is an income-plus-deleveraging holding (6.2% dividend yield, leverage 3.5x -> ~3x by end-2027), not a multi-bagger; the 15% hurdle is unreachable at any plausible price because 40% of enterprise value is debt, and the upside case requires synergies, a clean non-core exit and a return to positive volumes to all land.
key_judgments: FY2026 (first full Berry year) is the base year; FY2025 and earlier are a different company. The sanity check's FY2025 denominators are therefore harsh, but the fix was applied on its merits: the forward synergy credit was the real overstatement.
Margins are built from components with a cash haircut and, after the fix pass, credit only about a quarter of the remaining synergies in the base case.
No credit for the >$500m working-capital recovery, no charge for remaining integration cash costs, no divestiture proceeds -- all three are left out and roughly net to a small positive.
WACC 7.8% (7.3% standard build + 0.5% leverage/integration premium) held constant across scenarios; scenario-specific risk lives in the flows and the 25% bear weight.
Exit multiple capped at 15x owner FCF (~8x terminal EBITDA), below Amcor's 10-year EV/EBITDA minimum -- no re-rating of any kind is assumed.
